learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the graphical meaning of zeroes of a polynomial and master the relationship between these zeroes and their coefficients!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The highest power of 'x' in p(x) is the degree of the polynomial. Degree 1 = Linear, Degree 2 = Quadratic, Degree 3 = Cubic.
The zeroes of a polynomial p(x) are exactly the x-coordinates of the points where the graph of y = p(x) intersects the x-axis.
The graph of a quadratic polynomial (ax^2 + bx + c) is a U-shaped curve called a parabola. It opens upwards if 'a' is positive, and downwards if 'a' is negative.
If alpha (α) and beta (β) are the zeroes of ax^2 + bx + c, then: Sum of zeroes (α + β) = -b/a, and Product of zeroes (α × β) = c/a.
If you know the sum (S) and product (P) of zeroes, you can form the quadratic polynomial using the formula: k[x^2 - Sx + P].

fun_activity.title: 🎢 Rollercoaster Math
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a wavy rollercoaster track on a piece of paper. Draw an x-axis through it. Count how many times the track hits the ground (x-axis). That's how many 'zeroes' your rollercoaster polynomial has!

exam_tips: 📌 Finding the zeroes by splitting the middle term and verifying the relationship with coefficients is a highly repeated 3-mark question.
📌 Do not forget the constant 'k' when forming a polynomial: k(x^2 - (sum)x + product).
📌 To find the number of zeroes from a graph, carefully count ONLY the intersections on the x-axis, ignore the y-axis completely.
quick_recap: ⭐ A polynomial of degree 'n' can have at most 'n' real zeroes.
⭐ The sum of zeroes is related to the middle coefficient (-b/a).
⭐ The product of zeroes is related to the constant term (c/a).
